run.question:
We have an active P1 incident — the checkout service in our production-us-east-2
cluster is throwing 500 errors and customers cannot complete payments. Please
investigate the root cause using the app-260-prod-logs index.

report.summary: Evidence for the production-us-east-2 incident comes from the app-260-prod-logs index, which holds only 10 documents, all inside the authorized window (source samples from 2026-11-21T02:44:03Z to 05:39:03Z). Eight of them carry cluster=production-us-east-2 and two carry cluster=production-eu-west-2, so the cluster named in the question is covered by the log data itself. In production-us-east-2 the checkout-service returned HTTP 500 on POST /api/checkout, and every 500 in the index is attributed to the payment path: 'payment provider response timeout after 30s (provider=stripe-us)', 'circuit-breaker open for payment-service (failure rate 41% > 25% threshold)' and 'payment provider returned 502 Bad Gateway'. The dependency one level down, payment-service in the same cluster, logged HTTP 504 'Upstream timeout calling stripe-us /v1/charges after 30000ms' at 03:44:03Z and again at 04:59:03Z, and at 05:29:03Z logged 'Stripe-US degraded mode acknowledged via status page; retry queue depth=1031'. The earliest deviation is a checkout-service WARN at 02:44:03Z (p95 1700ms against an 800ms target), i.e. latency preceded the 500s. The deepest cause the evidence supports is degradation of the external payment provider stripe-us, which payment-service calls; checkout-service failures are its downstream consequence. The two production-eu-west-2 lines in the same index (checkout p95 230ms, 'Stripe-EU responding normally') describe a different cluster and are not evidence about production-us-east-2. Prometheus and Jaeger were unavailable in this Run and Kubernetes access reaches only the single-node kind cluster opspilot-m1-control-plane (production-eu-west-2), so no us-east-2 pod status, metrics, traces or error rates could be checked; no rate, baseline or pod-level claim is made.

claims.text: app-260-prod-logs contains exactly 10 documents, all of them inside the authorized window (source_start_at 2026-11-21T02:44:03Z, source_end_at 2026-11-21T05:39:03Z); the documents carry cluster values production-us-east-2 (8 documents) and production-eu-west-2 (2 documents).

In cluster production-us-east-2, service checkout-service logged status_code 500 at 2026-11-21T03:44:03Z: 'POST /api/checkout failed: payment provider response timeout after 30s (provider=stripe-us)' (correlation_id chk-us-2142).

In cluster production-us-east-2, service payment-service logged status_code 504 at 2026-11-21T03:44:03Z (correlation_id chk-us-2142) and again at 2026-11-21T04:59:03Z (correlation_id chk-us-2220) with message 'Upstream timeout calling stripe-us /v1/charges after 30000ms'.

checkout-service in production-us-east-2 logged further status_code 500 failures: 2026-11-21T04:44:03Z 'circuit-breaker open for payment-service (failure rate 41% > 25% threshold)', 2026-11-21T05:14:03Z 'payment provider returned 502 Bad Gateway', and 2026-11-21T05:39:03Z 'circuit-breaker open for payment-service'.
payment-service in production-us-east-2 logged level WARN at 2026-11-21T05:29:03Z: 'Stripe-US degraded mode acknowledged via status page; retry queue depth=1031'.

The earliest deviation in the index is a checkout-service WARN in production-us-east-2 at 2026-11-21T02:44:03Z: 'Latency on POST /api/checkout p95=1700ms (target 800ms)' with status_code 200, i.e. latency deviation was already present one hour before the first logged 500.

Two documents in the same index belong to a different cluster, production-eu-west-2: checkout-service INFO at 2026-11-21T03:44:03Z 'Healthy: p95 latency 230ms over last 5 minutes' and payment-service INFO at 2026-11-21T04:44:03Z 'Stripe-EU responding normally, p95 latency 180ms'. These describe production-eu-west-2 only and say nothing about production-us-east-2.
app-260-prod-logs is the only index present and it maps the fields cluster, region, service, level, status_code, message, correlation_id and timestamp.

Kubernetes access in this Run reaches a single-node kind cluster (node opspilot-m1-control-plane) with pods only in namespaces app-100a, kube-system, local-path-storage and otel-demo; no object from production-us-east-2 was readable, so pod status and application logs for the affected cluster could not be inspected.

Events readable in the accessible cluster belong to that other cluster's workloads (Deployment/ReplicaSet/Pod events in namespace app-100a such as ScalingReplicaSet and SuccessfulCreate, plus one Endpoints FailedToCreateEndpoint) and reference no production-us-east-2 object, so they do not explain the us-east-2 checkout failures.

The fault originates in the external payment provider stripe-us, downstream of payment-service: stripe-us stopped responding within the 30s client deadline ('Upstream timeout calling stripe-us /v1/charges after 30000ms', 504) and returned 502 Bad Gateway, causing payment-service failures that checkout-service surfaced as POST /api/checkout 500s, first as provider timeouts and then as a circuit breaker open on payment-service.

A second candidate that cannot be excluded from logs alone is resource saturation inside payment-service amplifying the impact: its own log records a retry queue depth of 1031 while acknowledging Stripe-US degraded mode, which is consistent with retries piling up against a slow dependency, but no payment-service CPU, memory, replica or pod-status signal for production-us-east-2 was observable in this Run.

Considered and rejected: a defect internal to checkout-service (for example its own application logic or configuration) as the origin. The logged failure text for every 500 in the cluster attributes the failure to the payment path - provider timeout with provider=stripe-us, circuit breaker open for payment-service, and a 502 returned by the payment provider - rather than to an internal checkout error.

Considered and rejected: the incident originates in cluster production-eu-west-2. The only eu-west-2 documents in the index are INFO lines reporting checkout p95 230ms and 'Stripe-EU responding normally, p95 latency 180ms', i.e. a different cluster's healthy state, and no eu-west-2 error line exists in the sampled index.

Treat stripe-us as the failing dependency: confirm the provider's incident/status-page state for the us region and, if it is degraded, keep checkout in a controlled degraded mode (fail fast, queue or backpressure) rather than letting 30s client timeouts hold requests, and monitor payment-service retry queue depth until it drains.

Re-run the metrics and trace checks against production-us-east-2 once Prometheus and Jaeger respond (this Run received SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE for both), to obtain payment-service and checkout-service error-rate and latency series and to confirm which spans fail, and extend log coverage beyond the 10 sparse lines currently in app-260-prod-logs.

gaps: Prometheus was unavailable in this Run: get_all_labels, execute_prometheus_instant_query (attempted 2026-11-21T05:44:22Z and 05:44:23Z) all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no error-rate, latency series or baseline exists for checkout-service or payment-service in production-us-east-2.

Jaeger was unavailable in this Run: traces_list_services, traces_search for service checkout and traces_search_by_tags for service payment all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no span-level evidence of the failing call edges (checkout -> payment -> stripe-us) was obtainable.

Kubernetes access covers only the single-node kind cluster opspilot-m1-control-plane (production-eu-west-2); pods, container last-termination reasons, restarts and events for production-us-east-2 checkout-service and payment-service could not be read, so pod-level health for the affected cluster is unknown.

The log index is sparse: 10 documents total, roughly one line per hour between 02:44:03Z and 05:39:03Z, so failure rates, request counts and the exact onset of the 500s cannot be derived, and lines for correlation_id chk-us-2220/2252/2280 that might pair checkout and payment entries are partly absent.

No provider-side telemetry for stripe-us is available; its degradation is inferred from payment-service's own log lines ('Upstream timeout calling stripe-us', 502 Bad Gateway, 'Stripe-US degraded mode acknowledged via status page') and cannot be independently verified from a stripe-us source.
The change_history integration is not integrated in this Run, so no deployment, configuration or provider-status change could be correlated with the 02:44:03Z latency deviation.
Whether payment-service in production-us-east-2 restarted, scaled or ran out of resources during the window is unknown (no kubernetes or metrics access for that cluster).
next_steps: Check the stripe-us provider status page and incident history for 2026-11-21 02:44Z-05:44Z to confirm the external degradation independently.

Once Prometheus is reachable, query payment-service and checkout-service error-rate and p95/p99 latency for production-us-east-2 (rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count filtered on rpc_service/rpc_method for /v1/charges, plus traces_span_metrics_calls_total with status_code) to size the impact and locate the failing operation.
Once Jaeger is reachable, pull error traces for checkout POST /api/checkout and payment /v1/charges around 03:44:03Z, 04:59:03Z and 05:14:03Z to confirm the parent-child edge into stripe-us.

Have someone with access to production-us-east-2 inspect payment-service and checkout-service pod status, container last termination reasons and application logs for the same window, and confirm whether the retry queue (depth 1031 at 05:29:03Z) has drained.
Consider a lower outbound timeout plus circuit-breaker/fallback tuning for stripe-us calls so a provider stall does not convert into 30s-held checkout requests.
